text:
maria: heads-up — canary rollout to int8 profile is showing a 20-30% p95 latency regression on a subset of traffic after today's scheduler/prefetch changes. rolling hold for now? :eyes:

akshay: saw the same in staging. bisect traces the delta to merge 7d3c2a9 (prefetcher: schedule window + kernel selection heuristics). can reproduce locally with loadgen.

perf-ci-bot: [ALERT] perf-regression detected on canary job `canary-int8-06`: p95 increased from 42ms -> 54ms (28%); p99 increased from 89ms -> 125ms. See job: https://ci.internal/redwood/job/canary-int8-06/174

jon: attaching quick perf summary from flamegraphs — mostly hotspots in dequant path and memcpy during KV cache refill. also batch coalescing has more small-batch churn.

lei: looks like prefetcher is evicting kv entries too eagerly when window=128 + aggressive kernel switch. KV miss rate jumps which forces dequant + memcpy on hot tokens. that chain adds both latency and CPU overhead.

maria: logs snippet from a canary request that shows the symptom:

```
[2026-02-08T15:12:03Z] request id=rc_8ef
route: int8-prefetch
batch_size: 8 -> 1 (coalesced->flushed)
kv_hit: false
dequant_time_ms: 2.34
memcpy_time_ms: 1.12
kernel_switch_ms: 0.78
total_token_ms: 4.24
```

akshay: local repro script (small load) shows same when `--prefetch-window=128`. with `--prefetch-window=32` p95 goes back to baseline. suspect race between prefetch scheduling and batcher coalesce timer.

lei: config we tested:
```
batcher.max_batch=64
batcher.coalesce_ms=3
prefetcher.enabled=true
prefetcher.window=128
kernel.selector.mode=aggressive
```

sarah: ran a microbench for the dequant path. results:
```
int8->fp16 dequant memcpy (hot path): 2.3ms/op
int8->fp16 domain-optimized path: 0.35ms/op
copy+convert fallback: 1.9ms/op
```

sarah: so two problems: (1) our fast path isn't being selected when prefetch triggers kernel change, (2) memcpy/fallback dominates when kv miss forces rehydrate.

akshay: plan: 1) hold rollout (done), 2) patch prefetcher to be less aggressive (window=32) and re-run canary, 3) add guard in kernel selector to prefer dequant fast-path stability for active caches, 4) add targeted unit benchmark for dequant+kv refill.

jon: I can iterate on the kernel selector guard — PR coming in ~30m. the guard will: if kv_hit_rate_recent < 0.8 then avoid switching to aggressive kernel for next N batches. reduces thrash.

maria: can we avoid a full revert? we prefer a config toggle to reduce blast radius. but if we can't get a config tuned quick, revert 7d3c2a9 and ship the selector guard behind a feature flag.

lei: ran the quick config toggle in staging: setting `prefetcher.window=32` dropped p95 from 54ms->44ms and reduced KV miss rate by ~60%. stable under 10k qps.

perf-ci-bot: rerun scheduled for staging with new config. jobs queued.

dev-bot: created PR #4892: "prefetcher: add tunable window + safety guard" and PR #4893: "kernel-selector: prefer stable dequant fast-path on low kv-hit".

akshay: timeline: if staging looks good in 30-45m we can roll forward with toggled config and ship the kernel guard behind feature flag for canary. if not, revert commit.

maria: thanks. please post short postmortem if revert happens. cc @sarah @lei for perf follow-ups. :thumbsup:

jon: quick note — adding microbenchmark and CI check for dequant hot-paths so we catch this in presubmit. will add to perf-nightly too.

sarah: I'll instrument KV refill counters and add telemetry so we can alert on sudden jumps in kv miss rate tied to config changes.

lei: staging results in: canary config change looks stable, promoting to partial rollout 10% now. monitoring closely.

maria: closing the hold only after 2 hours of stable partial rollout. everyone keep eyes on p95 and kv_miss metric.

akshay: noted. thanks team.
